source.file: hero-video-smoothed.mp4 (kept out of public/; skin pre-smoothed with smartblur)
source.subject: stylised man, curly brown hair, tattooed forearms, brown T-shirt, dark blue-grey background; slow push-in / lean toward the camera and three slow blinks

crop.why: full source height (hair top is only 4-48 px below the top edge, so any vertical crop would cut hair); width centred on the head/body axis with a slight bias that leaves look-room on the right, the direction he faces

framing.unitNote: fractions of the 4:5 output frame, measured across the whole clip
framing.tightHeadroom: by the last frames the outermost hair strands graze the top edge (the dense curls stay about 15-40 source px inside); give the frame a mat/border and do not crop any further from the top

timing.mapping: frame i is shown at t = i/24. Map pointer progress p in [0,1] to currentTime = p * 6 (NOT p * duration, which can land past the last frame). To snap: t = Math.round(p * 144) / 24.

motion.headDrift: very slow push-in / lean toward the camera: hair width grows about 12% (1068 -> 1204 px full-res) and the forearm span about 11% between frame 0 and frame 144; hair top rises from y=48 to y=4 px; head centre stays within +-12 px. The first ~0.3 s (frames 2-6) moves slightly faster as the head settles. Gaze stays fixed off-camera to the right. No clear periodic breathing motion was detected in the shoulder line (it drifts by under 2% of the frame height).
motion.loopNote: frame 0 and frame 144 differ (push-in), so a plain loop jump-cuts; use ping-pong (portrait-loop.mp4 or JS) instead

videos.notes: H.264 High L4.0, all-intra (every frame an IDR), crf 18 + tune film. Universal fallback for the scrub effect.
VP9 profile 0, all-intra (every frame a keyframe), crf 40. About 25% smaller than portrait.mp4 at equal-or-better SSIM/VMAF. List first, mp4 second.
H.264 High L3.1, all-intra, crf 20 + tune film. 640 px wide for phones and tight bandwidth.
VP9 all-intra, crf 46, 640 px wide. About 26% smaller than portrait-sm.mp4 at about the same SSIM.

OPTIONAL touch/no-hover fallback: seamless ping-pong loop (frames 0..144 then 143..1 = 288 frames = 12.0 s), long-GOP H.264, crf 20. NOT scrub-friendly (inter-coded); use only with autoplay muted loop playsinline.

posters.use: poster attribute for portrait.* (960x1200) and the static fallback
alternative still (eyes open, mid push-in): reduced-motion / hover-intent / share-image candidate

filmStrip.note: eyes are open in every thumbnail except f-06 (frame 65), which catches the second blink as the lids reopen; swap in frame 68 if all-open eyes are preferred. No sprocket artwork is baked in; draw the perforations in CSS.

css.objectPositionNote: only matters if the container is not 4:5. Wider than 4:5 (square, 4:3): cover trims top/bottom, so top-align (0%) to keep the hair and trim forearms. Narrower than 4:5 (3:4, 2:3): trims the sides; 48% keeps the head centred. Never use a y position above 0%.
css.placeholderNote: average of the dark blue-grey backdrop (corners about #17181d to #1f2024). Set it on the frame so nothing flashes white before the poster decodes.
css.videoAttributes: muted playsinline preload="none" disablepictureinpicture disableremoteplayback (no controls; no loop for the scrub version)
css.reserveSpace: set aspect-ratio: 4 / 5 on the frame (or width/height 960x1200) to avoid layout shift

usage.assetUrls: Vite base is '/', so '/about/portrait.webm' works; the safe form is `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}about/portrait.webm`
chooseSource: Do not rely on <source media=...> inside <video> (not honoured consistently); pick the file in JS.

Pointer devices (matchMedia('(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)')) on viewports wider than ~700 px with no saveData: portrait.webm if v.canPlayType('video/webm; codecs="vp09.00.40.08"') is truthy, else portrait.mp4.
Pointer devices on small viewports, navigator.connection.saveData, or effectiveType 2g/3g: portrait-sm.webm / portrait-sm.mp4 (same selection logic).
loading: Render the poster first (poster attribute or an ), keep preload="none", and set src + call load() when the frame is within about one viewport of the screen (IntersectionObserver, rootMargin ~600px).
Enable scrubbing only after readyState === 4 / 'canplaythrough' so the whole file is buffered; until then keep showing the poster.
Files are faststart (mp4) / cues-at-front (webm), so range requests and seeking work as soon as the header is fetched.
scrub: Listen to pointermove on the frame; p = (clientX - rect.left) / rect.width, clamped 0..1 (horizontal scrub reads as turning the head).
Smooth in a requestAnimationFrame loop: current += (target - current) * 0.18, then video.currentTime = current * 6. Skip the assignment when |delta| < 1/48 s or video.seeking is true.

Measured in desktop Chrome (local file, the four scrub files): seek-to-presented median about 7 ms (seeked event 2-4 ms), 0 wrong frames in 480 random seeks, and a 3 s sweep presented a frame on (almost) every one of ~432 rAF ticks while visiting 144-145 of the 145 frames. All-intra is why: no keyframe back-tracking.
Do not use fastSeek(); with all-intra files plain currentTime is already exact and cheap.
On pointerleave glide back to the resting frame (about 0) with the same smoothing instead of jumping.
touchFallback: Recommended for (hover: none) devices: <video autoplay muted loop playsinline poster=poster-sm.webp src=portrait-loop.mp4> (1.1 MB, seamless 12 s ping-pong). Cheaper than the 3.9 MB scrub file and needs no seeking on iOS.

Optional: also allow drag-to-scrub on touch by loading portrait-sm.* on first touch (touch-action: pan-y on the frame so vertical page scroll still works). Untested on iOS/Safari: seeking an unplayed video there can need a prior play()/pause(), which is why the loop file is the default.
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> show poster.webp / poster-sm.webp only (no autoplay loop, no auto-animation); pointer scrub is user-driven and may stay.
iOS Low Power Mode and some data-saver modes block autoplay: that is fine, the poster simply stays visible, so always set the poster.
A plain forward loop of portrait.* is NOT recommended (jump-cut from frame 144 back to 0).

encode.pipeline: hero-video-smoothed.mp4 -> crop=1732:2164:990:0 -> scale lanczos+accurate_rnd -> lossless FFV1 intermediate -> final encodes
encode.h264AllIntra: -c:v libx264 -preset veryslow -tune film -profile:v high -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 1 -keyint_min 1 -sc_threshold 0 -bf 0 -an -movflags +faststart (crf 18 for 960 px, crf 20 for 640 px)
encode.color: all video tagged BT.709 / limited (tv) range via setparams; posters and thumbnails converted YUV->RGB with the BT.709 matrix, so poster and video match (mean abs difference about 1.4 of 255 in Chrome)
